title: JSW Indian Open Returns With India's First Women's Silver-Level PSA Tournament
excerpt: The third edition runs February 9-13, 2027 at Mumbai Gymkhana, with the women's event upgraded to Silver level and the men remaining at Copper.
body:
• The JSW Indian Open returns for its third edition from February 9 to 13, 2027, at Mumbai Gymkhana, with the women's event upgraded to Silver level on the PSA World Tour.
  • The upgrade makes it India's first-ever women's Silver-level PSA tournament, while the men's competition remains at Copper level.
  • The announcement follows India's five-medal squash haul at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games, where Anahat Singh won silver in the women's singles.
  • The draw, participating players and ticketing details for the 2027 edition will be announced in due course, according to the organisers.

The JSW Indian Open will return for a third edition from February 9 to 13, 2027, at Mumbai Gymkhana, and the women's competition will be played at Silver level on the Professional Squash Association (PSA) World Tour for the first time. The upgrade makes the tournament India's first-ever women's Silver-level event on the circuit, according to the announcement reported by NDTV and The Bridge. The men's competition will remain at Copper level.

A Step Up for the Women's Game

Silver is a higher tier than the Copper status the women's event carried in the tournament's first two editions, and it brings a deeper international field and more ranking points to a home event. For Indian players, that means the chance to face stronger opposition without leaving the country, and to gain experience against the level of competition they otherwise meet only on tour overseas.

"Hosting India's first-ever women's Silver-level tournament on the PSA Tour is a significant milestone and reflects our commitment to creating stronger competitive opportunities for women in squash."

— Divyanshu Singh, CEO, JSW Sports

Singh said the success of the previous editions, coupled with India's performances at the Asian Games, gave the organisers momentum to bring the tournament back at a higher level in 2027, with the aim of strengthening India's presence on the international squash calendar.

Built on a Breakthrough Season

The announcement lands after a season in which Indian squash produced results across the tour. Anahat Singh's rise through the world rankings has led the new generation, alongside the progress of Abhay Singh, Ramit Tandon, Veer Chotrani and Velavan Senthilkumar. At the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games, India secured five squash medals — two silver and three bronze — with Anahat Singh taking silver in the women's singles and further medals coming across the team and doubles competitions.

The Indian Open itself has tracked that rise. The inaugural edition in 2025 was staged at Bombay Gymkhana and was named among the PSA's top events of the year. The second edition moved to the Cricket Club of India in March 2026, where Anahat Singh defended her title against Egypt's Hana Moataz and Abhay Singh beat Veer Chotrani in an all-Indian men's final. The 2027 edition returns to the Gymkhana setting with a higher ceiling for the women's draw.

The Road to Los Angeles

The timing matters beyond one tournament. Squash will make its Olympic debut at the Los Angeles 2028 Games, and home events at Silver and Copper level form part of the competitive pathway Indian players need in the two seasons before it — regular matches against international opposition, ranking points, and experience of five-day tour events. Manisha Malhotra, President of the Inspire Institute of Sport, said platforms such as the JSW Indian Open give athletes international exposure and the chance to benchmark themselves against leading players as they progress.

What the Silver upgrade will mean in prize money and draw strength is not yet public. The organisers said other details regarding participating players, the draw and ticketing for the 2027 edition will be announced in due course. The tournament's place on the calendar can be tracked on the PSA Squash Tour tournaments page.
